title: An Optical Illusion: High Electron Densities Create Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxy Impostors
headline: High Electron Densities Mimic Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxies: An Optical Illusion
tldr: JWST observations revealed galaxies that appear extremely metal-poor, but high electron densities can mimic low metallicity signatures. This study shows that careful analysis of ionized gas conditions is essential to avoid misclassifying galaxies as first-generation systems.
significance: The work cautions against overinterpreting low-metallicity signatures in early galaxies, refining the search for truly primordial galaxies.

title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
headline: ConceptGuard: A New Benchmark for Context‑Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: ConceptGuard introduces a realistic evaluation framework that tests LLMs’ ability to forget context‑dependent knowledge without compromising unrelated facts. It moves beyond simple fact recall, addressing the nuanced demands of real‑world unlearning.
significance: By revealing gaps in current unlearning methods, ConceptGuard pushes the development of safer, more controllable language models.

title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
headline: 4DAnyone: Reconstructing 4D Humans from Uncalibrated Monocular Video
tldr: 4DAnyone generates reconstruction‑grade, multiview‑consistent videos from a casual monocular clip and lifts them into 4D Gaussian Splatting, enabling 4D human reconstruction without camera calibration. It overcomes the view‑consistency limitations of existing diffusion models when scaling to dozens of target views.
significance: This framework democratizes high‑fidelity 4D human reconstruction, allowing realistic avatars to be created from everyday videos without specialized hardware.

title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
headline: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
tldr: WithEveryone introduces a unified framework that simultaneously plans spatial layout and grounds identities for group image generation, ensuring each specified person appears in the correct location with accurate facial features. The method aligns noisy predicted faces through training-time identity losses, improving reliability over existing models.
significance: This approach addresses a key limitation in multi-person image synthesis, enabling more accurate and scalable generation of complex scenes with multiple identities.

title: Swift-Image: Exploring the Performance Frontier of Compact Unified Image Generation Models
headline: Swift-Image: Compact Unified Diffusion Model for Text-to-Image and Editing
tldr: Swift-Image is a 6B single-stream DiT that unifies text-to-image generation and image editing in a single compact model. Through a progressive training pipeline and systematic engineering, it pushes the performance frontier while staying within a constrained computational budget.
significance: It demonstrates that small, efficient diffusion models can achieve competitive performance across multiple vision tasks, enabling broader deployment.

title: Production of quarkonium pairs via the fragmentation mechanism
headline: Fragmentation Mechanisms Drive Quarkonium Pair Production in High-Energy Collisions and Beyond
tldr: We analyze how fragmentation processes contribute to the production of quarkonium pairs in hadronic collisions. A microscopic perturbative model for dihadron fragmentation functions is developed to quantify the double-hadron mechanism.
significance: This work provides a quantitative framework for understanding quarkonium pair production, essential for interpreting LHC data and testing QCD factorization.

title: The Memory Hidden in Response Fluctuations: Trajectory-Level Fluctuation-Response Theory and Inequalities for Non-Markovian Jump Dynamics
headline: Memory Effects in Non-Markovian Jump Dynamics: A Trajectory-Level Fluctuation-Response Theory
tldr: We formulate a fluctuation-response framework for non-Markovian jump processes directly on the event record, deriving exact stochastic equations for transition counts. This approach reveals how memory destroys closed master equations yet still permits precise response inequalities.
significance: The work provides a rigorous tool to analyze memory-driven nonequilibrium systems, bridging trajectory statistics and response theory.

title: Competing triangular and stripe supersolid orders in a dipolar quantum gas
headline: Competing Triangular and Stripe Supersolid Orders Observed in a Dipolar Quantum Gas
tldr: Researchers have experimentally realized two distinct supersolid patterns—triangular and stripe—in a dipolar quantum gas. This observation confirms theoretical predictions and opens avenues for exploring exotic quantum phases.
significance: The discovery provides the first experimental evidence of competing spatial orders in dipolar supersolids, validating complex phase diagrams predicted by theory.

title: $TCP_α$: Margin-Controlled Confidence estimation for reliable Music Information Retrieval
headline: Margin‑Controlled Confidence Estimation for Reliable Music Retrieval
tldr: Deep neural networks often overestimate confidence, misleading users. The proposed TCP_α method trains a lightweight auxiliary head to generate more reliable confidence scores for music information retrieval tasks.
significance: TCP_α offers a practical, post‑hoc solution to improve trustworthiness of MIR predictions by controlling confidence margins.

title: Strange Metal Hall Effect in Underdoped BaFe$_2$(As$_{1-x}$P$_x$)$_2$
headline: Hall Effect Reveals Doping-Independent Behavior in Strange Metal BaFe2(As1−xPx)2
tldr: The study measures the Hall effect in underdoped BaFe2(As1−xPx)2 and finds a doping‑independent contribution that persists across a wide temperature range. This suggests a universal transport mechanism in strange metals beyond the quasiparticle picture.
significance: It provides new insight into the fundamental physics of high‑temperature superconductors by identifying a universal Hall response in the strange metal regime.

title: Spin-torque microwave detectors of positive rectangular pulse signals
headline: Spin-Torque Microwave Detectors Operate in Linear and Nonlinear Pulse Regimes
tldr: We study spin-torque microwave detectors driven by positive rectangular current pulses and identify linear and nonlinear operation regimes. The time-averaged voltage scales linearly with pulse amplitude in the linear regime and shows distinct behavior in the nonlinear regime.
significance: This work provides a framework for optimizing spin-torque detectors for high-speed microwave sensing applications.

title: A comparison between ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB and Wi-Fi radar for in-bedroom human activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection
headline: Comparing Ceiling-Mounted FMCW, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi Radar for Bedside Activity Monitoring
tldr: This study evaluates three RF sensing technologies—FMCW radar, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi—in identical bedroom setups to detect human activity and sleep interruptions. Results highlight trade-offs in accuracy, latency, and deployment complexity, guiding future contact‑free health monitoring systems.
significance: It provides the first side‑by‑side benchmark of these radar modalities under controlled conditions, informing design choices for non‑intrusive sleep and activity monitoring.

title: Probabilistic Representation and Convergence of Gromov-Wasserstein Gradient Flows
headline: Probabilistic Gromov–Wasserstein Gradient Flow Convergence
tldr: The paper derives a probabilistic representation for the inner product Gromov–Wasserstein gradient flow of relative entropy with respect to a Gaussian measure, proving convergence and connecting it to diffusion processes and PDEs.
significance: It links optimal transport theory with stochastic PDEs, providing new analytical tools for metric measure spaces.

title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
headline: SPADE: Self-Play RL for Adaptive Synthetic Environments with LLMs
tldr: SPADE introduces a self-play reinforcement learning framework that lets a single large language model generate and solve increasingly diverse synthetic goals. By continuously expanding its goal pool, the agent adapts to scaling challenges and improves performance without external supervision.
significance: This approach enables language agents to autonomously evolve their training curriculum, overcoming the limitations of static goal distributions.

title: Qualified Cross-References as a Verification Method: The Normative Environment of the EU AI Act
headline: Using Qualified Cross-References to Verify EU AI Act Compliance Framework
tldr: The paper proposes a method for representing legal cross-references with qualified links that capture legal character, supporting provisions, and conditions. This approach ensures consistency and verifiability across the EU AI Act’s normative environment.
significance: It offers a systematic way to encode and verify legal relationships, enhancing transparency and compliance in AI governance.

title: The Structured Totient Preimage Problem: Reconstruction, Collisions, and Cryptographic Implications
headline: Reconstructing Primes from Totient Products: The Structured Totient Preimage Problem
tldr: The Structured Totient Preimage (STP) problem asks to recover k distinct λ‑bit primes given only the product of their decremented values, x = ∏(p_i−1). While verifiable efficiently, the problem’s reconstruction hardness has implications for cryptographic constructions.
significance: STP provides a new hard problem that could underpin cryptographic primitives and offers insight into prime reconstruction challenges.

title: SiNMULI: Novel Signed Network Approach for Malicious URL Identification
headline: SiNMULI: Signed Network Model Enhances Detection of Malicious URLs in Real-Time
tldr: SiNMULI introduces a novel signed network framework that captures relationships between URLs and user interactions, improving phishing detection accuracy. The model leverages graph-based features and achieves state‑of‑the‑art performance on benchmark datasets.
significance: By modeling malicious URL propagation as a signed network, SiNMULI offers a scalable, interpretable solution that outperforms traditional machine‑learning classifiers.

title: PartialBiGrasp: Inferring Hidden Local Geometry for Bimanual Grasping from Partial Views
headline: PartialBiGrasp: Inferring Hidden Geometry for Dual-Arm Grasping from Partial Views
tldr: PartialBiGrasp introduces a method to infer hidden local geometry for bimanual grasping using only partial point cloud views. By predicting sparse graspable regions from incomplete data, it enables dual-arm robots to manipulate large, complex objects that were previously ungraspable with single-arm approaches.
significance: This approach expands the capability of dual-arm robots to handle large, geometrically complex objects by overcoming the limitation of incomplete sensor data.

title: Diffuse HI emission in the circumgalactic medium of NGC891 and NGC4565 - III: azimuthal profiles
headline: Azimuthal Profiles of Diffuse HI Emission in the CGM of NGC891 and NGC4565
tldr: The study maps the inner neutral circumgalactic medium around NGC891 and NGC4565, revealing a 360° view of HI inflows and co-rotation within 25–30 kpc. It confirms that minor‑axis inflows and major‑axis co‑rotation persist across the full azimuthal range.
significance: These observations provide the most complete azimuthal characterization of neutral gas in nearby galaxy halos, refining models of gas accretion and disk–halo interaction.

title: A Fast Deterministic Algorithm for $(Δ+1)$-edge coloring in CONGEST
headline: Deterministic (Δ+1)-Edge Coloring Achieved in Polylogarithmic Rounds on CONGEST in Distributed Setting
tldr: A recent deterministic algorithm finds a (Δ+1)-edge coloring in poly(Δ, log n) rounds in the CONGEST model, improving upon previous randomized methods. The technique leverages new combinatorial insights to overcome communication bottlenecks.
significance: This result demonstrates that optimal edge coloring can be achieved deterministically in near-linear time on distributed networks, closing a long-standing gap between theory and practice.

title: The regular pentagon is canonically Ramsey
headline: Canonical Ramsey Property of the Regular Pentagon Revealed
tldr: Researchers proved that any colouring of a sufficiently large point set contains either a monochromatic or rainbow copy of a regular pentagon. This extends the canonical Ramsey theory beyond triangles to more complex polygons.
significance: The result deepens our understanding of geometric configurations in combinatorial geometry, showing that even regular pentagons exhibit canonical Ramsey behaviour.

title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
headline: Hydra-0: Generalist World Model Using Action Flow for Cross-Embodiment Control
tldr: We present Hydra-0, a generalist world model that encodes robot actions as pixel motion, enabling shared visual interfaces across embodiments and tasks. The model achieves significant reductions in robot- and object-motion error compared to prior methods.
significance: Hydra-0 demonstrates that action flow can unify world modeling and control across diverse robots and environments, paving the way for more adaptable autonomous systems.

title: From Corpora to Co-Evolving Capabilities: Capability-Centric Data Design for Generalist Image Generation
headline: Designing Data for Generalist Image Generation: A Capability-Centric Pipeline Approach
tldr: The paper introduces a new data design paradigm that aligns heterogeneous supervision with interdependent generative capabilities, enabling more efficient training of generalist image generation models. By curating corpora in a capability-centric manner, the authors demonstrate improved performance across multiple generation tasks compared to conventional task-specific datasets.
significance: This work provides a scalable framework for building versatile image generation systems that can adapt to diverse tasks without retraining separate models.

title: Analytic Continuation of Conformal Integrals in Momentum Space
headline: Analytic Continuation of Conformal Triple‑K Integrals for Higher‑Point Correlators in Momentum Space
tldr: This work extends the analytic continuation of triple‑K integrals, key building blocks of conformal correlators, to arbitrary complex dimensions. The results provide a systematic framework for evaluating higher‑point functions in momentum space.
significance: It offers a unified method to compute conformal correlators, enhancing our ability to test holographic dualities and conformal bootstrap techniques.

title: Multi-Agent AI System for Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance with Independent Radiologist Evaluation
headline: Multi-Agent AI System Enhances Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance
tldr: We developed a locally deployed multi-agent AI pipeline that structures and verifies radiology reports from CT scans. Evaluation on 638 reports from 15 radiologists shows improved consistency and reduced errors.
significance: This study demonstrates that a multi-agent AI framework can reliably standardize radiology documentation, potentially improving clinical workflow and patient safety.

title: Ultrafast and high resolution spatial light modulation for cold atoms
headline: Ultrafast, High-Resolution Spatial Light Modulation Enables Precise Control of Cold Atom Arrays
tldr: A new ultrafast spatial light modulator provides high-resolution optical shaping, allowing precise local control of programmable ultracold atom arrays. This advancement accelerates quantum computation and simulation by enabling rapid, accurate manipulation of atomic qubits.
significance: The technology dramatically improves the scalability and fidelity of quantum processors based on cold atoms.

title: Revisiting the Intra-Team Communication Method to Elicit Level-k Reasoning in Beauty Contests and 11-20 Games
headline: Revisiting Intra-Team Communication for Level‑k Reasoning in Beauty Contests and 11‑20 Games
tldr: We use intra‑team communication to uncover level‑0 strategies in beauty contests and 11‑20 games. The results show how higher‑level players evaluate these baseline actions.
significance: It advances understanding of bounded rationality by linking communication methods to level‑k modeling.

title: Planning Against Learning in Rank-1 Games
headline: Strategic Planning Against Learners in Rank‑1 Games: Optimizing for Replicator Dynamics
tldr: In repeated multi‑agent settings, a player can anticipate and shape a learner’s future actions by planning against the learner’s adaptation dynamics. The paper shows that optimizing against the continuous‑time Replicator Dynamics is computationally tractable for rank‑1 games.
significance: This work bridges game theory and online learning, enabling opponents to strategically influence learning agents in a tractable manner.

title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
headline: Assessing the Reliability and Fragility of Memory‑Based Self‑Improving Agents in Online Learning
tldr: This study re‑examines two memory‑based self‑improving agents, revealing significant variance due to task order and underspecification. The findings highlight the need for robust benchmarks and clearer specifications to ensure reliable performance.
significance: It underscores that without careful evaluation, self‑improving agents may exhibit unpredictable behavior, jeopardizing their deployment.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Preconditioning for Stable Training of Recurrent Neural Quantum States
headline: Stabilizing Recurrent Neural Quantum States with Quantum Geometric Tensor Preconditioning
tldr: This work introduces a preconditioning scheme based on the quantum geometric tensor to mitigate instability in training recurrent neural quantum states. Experiments demonstrate improved convergence and accuracy for ground-state estimation in many-body systems.
significance: The method enables reliable training of autoregressive neural quantum states, advancing scalable quantum many-body simulations.

title: EDITBRIDGE: Towards Faithful and Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Image Editing
headline: EDITBRIDGE: Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Diffusion Editing Without Two-Stage Pipelines for Professional Workflows
tldr: EDITBRIDGE introduces a novel diffusion-based framework that directly edits images at resolutions exceeding 4K, bypassing the memory bottleneck of traditional attention mechanisms. The method achieves high fidelity and speed, outperforming conventional two-stage low-resolution editing plus super-resolution pipelines on benchmark datasets.
significance: By enabling faithful, efficient editing at ultra-high resolutions, EDITBRIDGE advances professional image processing and opens new possibilities for large-scale visual content creation.

title: TokEval: A Tokenizer Evaluation Suite
headline: TokEval: A Comprehensive Suite for Evaluating Language Model Tokenizers and Their Impact
tldr: TokEval introduces a set of metrics that assess tokenizer design choices beyond token count, providing insights into how these choices influence downstream LLM performance. By offering a systematic evaluation framework, TokEval helps practitioners select tokenizers that align with specific model capabilities and application needs.
significance: This framework enables more informed tokenizer selection, potentially improving LLM efficiency and effectiveness across diverse tasks.

title: The concentration game: Bayesian updating, regret, and information
headline: Bayesian Updating Meets Regret Minimization in a Two-Player Zero-Sum Game
tldr: We present a zero-sum repeated game where a learner updates beliefs via Bayesian inference while minimizing exponential-weight regret. The framework unifies concentration inequalities by linking terminal payoff to the maximum gain achievable under a fixed relative entropy constraint.
significance: This work bridges game theory, Bayesian learning, and concentration results, offering a unified perspective on adaptive decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Delegation Asymmetry in Agentic Recommender Systems: Measuring Two-Sided Receptivity in Online Dating
headline: When Users Accept Agentic Dating: Measuring Two‑Sided Receptivity in Online Matchmaking
tldr: Autonomous LLM agents are increasingly used to converse on behalf of users in dating apps, but their success hinges on users’ willingness to both delegate and receive agent‑mediated messages. Our survey of 2,894 active users reveals a significant asymmetry in receptivity, highlighting the need for balanced design in agentic recommender systems.
significance: Understanding this asymmetry is crucial for designing effective and user‑acceptable agentic matchmaking platforms.

title: HLSR: Hybrid Live Forecast Selective Dynamic Vehicle Rerouting for Real-Time Congestion Avoidance
headline: Hybrid Live-Forecast Vehicle Rerouting for Real-Time Congestion Avoidance
tldr: Urban traffic congestion hampers productivity and raises costs. HLSR selectively reroutes vehicles by combining live edge speeds with short-horizon forecasts, improving real-time routing efficiency.
significance: HLSR offers a practical, scalable solution that balances computational load with routing accuracy, enabling smarter traffic management in real-world settings.

title: Don't Drop the BATON: Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Agentic Subtask Exploration and Transition-aware Memory
headline: LLM-Powered Subtask Planning Boosts Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation by Freezing Vision-Language Models
tldr: The authors freeze vision-language-action models and let an LLM agent plan subtask sequences in language. This approach reduces error compounding and allows robots to execute long-horizon manipulation chains more reliably.
significance: It demonstrates that LLM-driven subtask planning can overcome limitations of end-to-end VLA models in complex, multi-stage robotic tasks.

title: Q-based Variational Inverse Reinforcement Learning
headline: Q-Based Variational Inverse Reinforcement Learning: A Bayesian Approach to Preference Inference
tldr: Q-based Variational IRL (QVIRL) introduces a Bayesian framework that infers reward functions from expert behavior using Q-functions. The method improves safety and alignment in AI by learning human preferences more efficiently.
significance: QVIRL offers a principled way to align AI systems with human values, enhancing both safety and performance.

title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
headline: Training Pixel-Space Diffusion Models to Rival Latent Counterparts: An Empirical Guide
tldr: This study presents a practical recipe for training pixel-space text-to-image diffusion models that match or surpass latent-space models. Through extensive experiments, the authors identify key architectural and training choices that yield state-of-the-art performance.
significance: It bridges the gap between pixel-space and latent-space diffusion, providing a reproducible framework for high-quality image generation.

title: Evaluating Beyond the Screen: Collective Assessment of AI-Generated Business Plans with Resource-Constrained Entrepreneurs
headline: Collective Assessment of AI-Generated Business Plans for Resource-Constrained Entrepreneurs in Emerging Markets
tldr: Entrepreneurs rely on generative AI for critical documents, but errors can jeopardize funding. This study explores collaborative evaluation methods beyond the screen to improve accuracy for resource-constrained users.
significance: The research offers a scalable framework for improving AI-generated business plan reliability, crucial for small business financing.

title: $τ_0$-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation
headline: τ0-VLA: Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with Adaptive Test-Time Computation for Long-Horizon Tasks
tldr: τ0-VLA introduces a hierarchical vision-language-action framework that allocates extra computation to challenging decisions, improving long-horizon robot manipulation. By leveraging a world model at test time, it dynamically balances speed and accuracy for complex tasks.
significance: This approach enables more reliable and efficient robot planning by adaptively investing computational resources where they matter most.

title: Simplicial Actions for Distributed Protocols
headline: Simplicial Action Models for Distributed Protocols: Advancing Modal Logic in Complex Systems
tldr: This paper extends the semantics of belief revision in simplicial complexes by integrating action models, enabling dynamic epistemic reasoning in distributed protocols. The authors demonstrate how these models capture protocol updates and provide a framework for analyzing knowledge evolution in multi-agent systems.
significance: By bridging simplicial semantics with action models, the work offers a novel tool for formal verification of distributed protocols, enhancing robustness and transparency.

title: Spectral Gaps of Hit-and-Run and Coordinate Hit-and-Run
headline: Spectral Gap Bounds for Hit-and-Run and Coordinate Hit-and-Run in Convex Bodies
tldr: The paper establishes a lower bound on the spectral gap of the Hit‑and‑Run algorithm in terms of the Poincaré constant of the target distribution over a convex body. It also extends the analysis to the Coordinate Hit‑and‑Run variant, yielding similar convergence guarantees.
significance: These results provide the first rigorous mixing time bounds for Hit‑and‑Run in high dimensions, improving our understanding of random walk sampling algorithms.

title: On the relations between several notions of symmetry for the second order linear differential equation
headline: Symmetry Correspondence in Second-Order Linear ODEs
tldr: The paper establishes explicit links between Lie point, vertical, and operator symmetries for second-order linear differential equations, and describes the Lie algebra of infinite symmetries.
significance: It unifies disparate symmetry concepts, facilitating deeper analysis of linear ODEs.

title: Size matters more than packing in bimodal colloidal gel compositions
headline: Particle Size Trumps Packing in Bimodal Colloidal Gels
tldr: Simulations of bimodal colloidal gels with a 1:2 size ratio show that increasing the proportion of large particles enhances gel strength more than changes in local packing density. The study highlights particle size as the dominant factor in determining mechanical properties of depletion gels.
significance: This work challenges the conventional focus on packing density, emphasizing particle size as the key design parameter for colloidal gel formulations.

title: Impression Share Prediction: An Offline Evaluation Task for Ranking Systems
headline: Predicting Impression Share: Offline Evaluation for Ranking System Effectiveness
tldr: Offline metrics often miss how ranking models shift impression distribution, potentially harming downstream outcomes. This paper proposes a method to predict impression share shifts, enabling better pre-deployment assessment.
significance: Accurately forecasting impression share changes allows practitioners to avoid costly online failures and align models with business goals.

title: Biophysics-informed deep operator learning for inverse problems with application to electrophysiological source reconstruction
headline: Deep Operator Learning Illuminates Neural Source Reconstruction from Noisy Brain Signals
tldr: By integrating biophysical constraints into deep operator networks, researchers can more accurately recover hidden neural activity from indirect, noisy measurements. This approach improves the stability and speed of electrophysiological source reconstruction.
significance: It offers a robust, physics-informed framework that could enhance real-time brain mapping for clinical and research applications.

title: Data-Efficient and Interpretable Classification of Circulating Tumor Cell Phenotypes in Microfluidic Devices via Deep Learning
headline: Data-Efficient Deep Learning Classifies Tumor Cell Phenotypes from Microfluidic Trajectories
tldr: The study presents a data‑efficient deep‑learning framework that interprets the kinematic trajectories of circulating tumor cells in microfluidic obstacle courses to classify phenotypes. By leveraging limited labeled data and explainable model components, it offers a rapid, label‑free diagnostic tool for metastatic potential assessment.
significance: This approach enables rapid, interpretable phenotyping of circulating tumor cells without labeling, potentially accelerating personalized cancer diagnostics.

title: Blazar Boosted Dark Matter in IceCube
headline: IceCube Probes Blazar-Boosted Dark Matter with 324 Blazar Sample
tldr: We evaluate IceCube's sensitivity to dark matter accelerated by blazar jets, modeling 324 blazars with inferred proton spectra. Our analysis shows that conservative dark matter spike profiles still allow detectable neutrino fluxes, setting new constraints on fermionic dark matter with vector mediators.
significance: This study links high-energy astrophysics and particle physics, offering a novel probe of dark matter interactions via blazar environments.

title: Forging Self-Funded Marketplaces among Strategic Agents
headline: Designing Incentive Mechanisms for Self-Funded Marketplaces Among Strategic Agents in Competitive Environments
tldr: We study how to design mechanisms that motivate agents to invest effort in a marketplace that they collectively fund. By modeling effort costs and revenues, we characterize conditions under which self-sustaining equilibria exist.
significance: This work provides foundational insights for building decentralized platforms where participants jointly finance and sustain economic activity.

title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
headline: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive, Practical, Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing Models
tldr: CPI-Bench introduces a comprehensive, practical, and intelligent benchmark designed to evaluate image editing models in real-world scenarios. It expands beyond single-image tasks, offering diverse coverage dimensions to better differentiate performance across advanced models.
significance: By providing a more realistic assessment framework, CPI-Bench accelerates the deployment of cutting-edge image editing technologies in practical applications.

title: Compressive Domains and a Bound for the Number of Components of the Fixed Locus of a Self-Map of the Berkovich Line
headline: Bound on Fixed Locus Components via Compressive Domains
tldr: We define compressive domains for rational maps on the Berkovich line, show they contain a classical fixed point, and use this to bound the number of connected components of the fixed locus.
significance: Provides a sharp upper bound on fixed locus components, advancing understanding of dynamics on nonarchimedean analytic spaces.

title: Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils
headline: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Decodes Sex of Prehistoric Hand Stencil Artists
tldr: We present a deep learning framework that incorporates uncertainty estimation to classify the biological sex of artists who created Upper Paleolithic hand stencils, overcoming challenges like lack of ground truth and image degradation. The model leverages transfer learning from contemporary populations and outputs probabilistic predictions, offering a robust tool for archaeologists.
significance: This approach provides archaeologists with a statistically grounded method to infer gender roles in prehistoric societies, bridging a critical gap in cultural anthropology.

title: Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking
headline: Leveraging LLMs for Semantics-Aware Type-Checking and Improved Vulnerability Detection in Complex Codebases
tldr: Traditional static analysis relies on syntactic rules, missing semantic cues like variable names. This study introduces an LLM-augmented type-checker that captures semantic context, improving vulnerability detection accuracy.
significance: By integrating LLMs, the approach bridges the gap between syntax and semantics, enabling more precise security analysis.

title: Trust Without Boundaries: An Architectural Analysis of Satellite Flight Software
headline: Breaking the Trust Barrier: Analyzing Satellite Flight Software Architecture for Secure Operations
tldr: Onboard flight software is a critical security boundary in modern spacecraft. Our analysis of NASA's Core Flight Software reveals that treating components as trusted peers limits isolation and access control, exposing vulnerabilities.
significance: Understanding these architectural weaknesses is essential for designing resilient, secure satellite systems.

title: All-optical switching of nonlinear structured light in crystal-engineered van der Waals materials
headline: All-Optical Switching of Structured Light via Nonlinear Van der Waals Crystals
tldr: Researchers demonstrate ultrafast, all-optical control of orbital angular momentum modes using engineered van der Waals crystals. This approach enables compact, real-time switching of structured light without bulky free‑space optics.
significance: The technique paves the way for scalable, nanoscale photonic devices capable of dynamic OAM manipulation, critical for next‑generation optical communications and quantum information processing.

title: Insight into SRF cavity performance from simulations of Nb's surface oxide dissolution and diffusion
headline: Simulating Nb Oxide Dissolution to Predict SRF Cavity Performance in Accelerators
tldr: We simulate the dissolution and diffusion of niobium oxide layers in vacuum, linking the resulting oxygen distribution to the superconducting performance of SRF cavities. These insights help optimize surface preparation for particle accelerators.
significance: This work bridges the gap between surface chemistry and SRF cavity performance, guiding more efficient accelerator designs.

title: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization
headline: SAEVerbalizer: Interpreting Sparse Autoencoder Features from LLM Representations for Transparent Insights
tldr: Sparse autoencoders extract many features from LLM embeddings, but explaining them usually relies on external observations, which can be superficial and computationally heavy. SAEVerbalizer offers a framework that verbalizes these features directly from representations, enabling efficient and deeper explanations.
significance: It provides a scalable, model-agnostic method to generate meaningful explanations for high-dimensional LLM features, improving transparency and trust.

title: Joint Communication-Control Strategy Optimization with Partially Nested Information Structures: The Linear-Quadratic Case
headline: Optimizing Joint Communication and Control in Multi-Agent Linear Systems with Partially Nested Information
tldr: The paper formalizes a joint communication–control strategy optimization problem for multi-agent linear systems with quadratic costs within the common-information-based framework. By focusing on partially nested information structures, it derives tractable, optimal solutions for the linear–quadratic case.
significance: It bridges decentralized control and communication design, enabling efficient coordination in multi-agent systems with limited information.

title: Non-uniqueness of Brakke flows starting from minimal surfaces with singularities
headline: Non-uniqueness of Brakke Flows from Singular Minimal Surfaces in Euclidean Space
tldr: We prove that minimal surfaces with singularities can generate multiple distinct Brakke flows. This demonstrates their dynamical instability.
significance: This result reveals that stationary varifolds need not uniquely determine their evolution, challenging assumptions in geometric measure theory.

title: The sensitivity of TESS to transiting planets in TOIs with close-in stellar companions
headline: TESS Transit Detection Sensitivity Affected by Close Stellar Companions in TOI Candidates
tldr: High-resolution imaging shows many TESS targets have close stellar companions that dilute transit signals. This study quantifies the impact on detecting small planets across 2052 TOIs, revealing reduced sensitivity in blended systems.
significance: Understanding companion-induced dilution is crucial for accurate planet occurrence rates from TESS.
